name: Toolweather
description: Is this MCP server healthy and safe to call now? Live checks of ~2,000 servers + alternatives. Also checks AI/dev API status, model deprecations, and scores a planned spend before an agent pays (SpendGate).
author: toolweather

tools.name: check_mcp_server_health
tools.title: Is this MCP server healthy / safe to call right now?
tools.description: Read whether one remote MCP server, and optionally one tool on it, is safe to call right now. Use before adding or calling that server, or after its calls fail or time out. Do not use it to search by capability (find_alternative_mcp_servers), to vet a list (batch_check_mcp_servers; stored verdicts only), or to subscribe to later outages (watch_server). A result older than 5 minutes, or fresh/bearer_token, runs one read-only initialize and spends a live-check credit (200/day, then the cache). Counts on the Toolweather quota (1,000/key or 50/day anonymous). Returns summary, verdict (safe|caution|unsafe|unknown), recommended_action (call_it|call_with_care|use_alternative|verify_yourself), reasons, latency_ms, auth, last_tool_change, checked_at, and freshness. Also callable as is_safe_to_call.

server.description: Registry name (io.github.owner/name) or that server's MCP endpoint URL. Partial names match the Toolweather index. A product homepage usually will not match.

tool.description: Optional tool name on that server. If the server is up but this name is absent, verdict is unsafe. Omit to judge the server only.

fresh.description: True forces a live read-only initialize now and spends one of 200 live checks/day (priced as a live check). Omit to live-check only when the stored result is older than 5 minutes.

bearer_token.description: Token for the target server only, not a Toolweather key. One authenticated initialize + tools/list, never stored or logged. Setting it forces a live check.

tools.name: find_alternative_mcp_servers
tools.title: Find a working MCP server that does X
tools.description: Search the Toolweather index for healthy MCP servers by capability, or for a replacement for one broken server. Use when check_mcp_server_health is unsafe or unknown, or when you lack a capability. Do not use it to judge one server you already chose (check_mcp_server_health) or to subscribe to later outages (watch_server). Does not call those servers and does not spend a live-check credit; unsafe rows are dropped. Returns summary, checked_at, and alternatives[] with server, url, verdict, latency_ms, and matching_tools. Counts on the Toolweather daily quota. Also callable as suggest_alternatives.

query.description: Capability phrase such as 'send email', or the registry name/URL of a server to replace. Not a tool name on Toolweather itself.

limit.description: Max ranked servers to return. Integer 1-20; omitted means 5. There is no paging cursor.

tools.name: get_api_key
tools.title: Get a free Toolweather API key
tools.description: Mint one new Toolweather API key (tw_…) for health checks and watches on this server (1,000 calls/day, 3 watches). Use it once per install, then send that key as the X-API-Key header. Do not call it every turn, and do not use it when you need a SpendGate key (spendgate_get_api_key returns sg_live_…). Takes no arguments; the caller network is the limit. Each call creates a different secret. Returns api_key once, plus daily_limit and watches_limit; later calls cannot fetch it again. A few new keys per network per day, then reuse an existing key. Health checks also work with no key at 50 calls/day.

tools.name: watch_server
tools.title: Alert me when an MCP server breaks
tools.description: Create one HTTPS webhook subscription for an indexed MCP server's verdict, auth requirement, or breaking tool-list change. Use instead of polling check_mcp_server_health. Do not use it to read health now (check_mcp_server_health) or to list subscriptions (list_watches). Requires a Toolweather key from get_api_key. The same server and webhook_url do not create a second watch; a different URL does. Three watches are free; each extra watch is $0.05 for 30 days via x402. Returns id and a one-time secret for the signature header. Toolweather later POSTs alerts to the webhook_url you supply. Does not spend the daily check quota.

server.description: Registry name (io.github.owner/name) or that server's MCP endpoint URL. Partial names match the Toolweather index. A product homepage usually will not match.

webhook_url.description: Public https URL Toolweather will POST JSON alerts to. Private, loopback, and non-https hosts are rejected. The same URL plus server does not create a second watch.

tools.name: list_watches
tools.title: List my server watches
tools.description: List webhook subscriptions stored for the Toolweather API key on this request, including delivery health. Use to copy a watch id before unwatch_server, or to see failures. Do not use it to learn if a server is up (check_mcp_server_health) or to create a subscription (watch_server). No arguments and no quota charge. The key is the X-API-Key header; anonymous callers are rejected. Returns watches[] (id, server, webhook_url, active, disabled_reason, last_known, consecutive_failures, last_delivery) and free_tier. Does not reveal webhook secrets and does not probe servers.

tools.name: unwatch_server
tools.title: Stop watching a server
tools.description: Delete one webhook subscription for this Toolweather API key and drop its pending deliveries. Use to stop alerts or to free a watch slot. Do not use it to change a webhook URL (delete, then watch_server) or to check health (check_mcp_server_health). Pass id from list_watches, not a server name. Repeating the same id deletes nothing further and returns watch not found. Returns {deleted: id}. Requires get_api_key first. Does not contact the MCP server and does not spend check quota.

id.description: Watch id from list_watches (w_…). Not a server registry name. An unknown id returns watch not found and removes nothing else.

tools.name: check_api_status
tools.title: Is this API / provider down right now?
tools.description: Read whether one tracked AI or developer API provider is operational, degraded, or down. Use before calling that provider, or right after 5xx, 429, or timeouts. Do not use it for an MCP server (check_mcp_server_health) or a model id (check_model_deprecation); ids come from list_providers, not URLs. Does not invoke the provider's API. Returns summary, verdict, recommended_action, open incidents, affected components, checked_at, and freshness (about every 4 minutes). Uses Upstream's quota, then $0.003 via x402, not the Toolweather check quota. Also callable as get_status.

provider.description: Lowercase id from list_providers, such as openai, anthropic, google-ai, github, or stripe. Not a URL and not an MCP registry name.

tools.name: check_model_deprecation
tools.title: Is this model deprecated, and what replaces it?
tools.description: Read whether one LLM model id is active, deprecated, or retired, plus its shutdown date and the provider's replacement. Use before hard-coding a model id, or when a call fails as model-not-found. Do not use it to see if the provider is down (check_api_status) or to list many retirements (list_recent_api_changes). Prefer model; id is only the legacy argument name. Returns summary, verdict, recommended_action (keep_using|plan_migration|switch_now|verify_with_provider), replacement, shutdown_date, evidence, and freshness. Upstream quota, then $0.003 via x402. Also callable as get_model.

model.description: Model id exactly as the provider API expects, such as gpt-4o or claude-3-opus-20240229. Not a provider name; that is check_api_status.

id.description: Legacy name for the same model id. Prefer model. Not a provider id.

tools.name: list_recent_api_changes
tools.title: What changed recently in AI/dev APIs?
tools.description: List recent outages, deprecation-page edits, model retirements, and pricing-page edits across tracked AI and developer APIs. Use to see what changed in a window, or to explain a sudden integration error. Do not use it for one provider's live status (check_api_status) or for the once-a-day narrative (get_digest). Returns summary plus items with timestamps and source links. Upstream quota, then $0.01 via x402. Also callable as get_changes.

since.description: ISO 8601 lower bound. Omit for the last 7 days. Not a YYYY-MM-DD digest key; that is get_digest's date.

provider.description: Optional id from list_providers. Omit to span every tracked provider.

kind.description: Optional change class. Omit for every class. Not a provider id.

limit.description: Max rows to return. Default 100, max 500. Not a page token.

tools.name: list_providers
tools.title: List tracked API providers
tools.description: List the AI and developer API providers Upstream tracks, each with state (operational, degraded, or outage) and checked_at. Use to choose a provider id before check_api_status. Do not use it as an MCP health check (check_mcp_server_health) or as the change feed (list_recent_api_changes). No arguments. Returns the catalog only. Does not probe providers, spend a SpendGate score, or use the Toolweather check quota. Free.

tools.name: get_digest
tools.title: Daily AI/dev API breaking-changes digest
tools.description: Read one daily digest of AI/dev API incidents, model retirements, pricing-page edits, and breaking MCP server changes. Use once a day instead of polling list_recent_api_changes. Do not use it for a live provider check (check_api_status) or a filtered change feed (list_recent_api_changes). Omit date for the latest issue. Returns that issue's summary and items. Free: no Toolweather quota and no webhook.

date.description: UTC day YYYY-MM-DD of one digest issue. Omit for the latest issue. Not an ISO timestamp and not a range.

tools.name: score_spend
tools.title: Score a planned spend before an agent pays
tools.description: Score one planned payment and return approve, ask_human, or block before any tool sends money. Use before a crypto transfer, gift card, subscription, or paid API call. Do not use it for uptime (check_mcp_server_health, check_api_status) or to read remaining free scores (get_quota). Does not transfer funds. Returns score 0-100, verdict (approve means pay, ask_human means stop and ask a person, block means do not pay), reasons, and recommended_action. Scoring is deterministic, so rewording purpose will not change the verdict. amount is USD, not token units. api_key, when set, is a SpendGate sg_live_ key, not a Toolweather tw_ key from get_api_key. Uses SpendGate's quota (100/day anonymous, 1,000/day with an sg_live_ key), then $0.001 via x402, not the Toolweather check quota.

amount.description: Planned spend in USD, not in token atomic units. Compared with daily_budget_remaining and monthly_budget_remaining when those are set.

currency.description: Payment currency. Defaults to USDC. Does not convert amount; amount stays in USD.

category.description: One of status_check, api_call, saas, infra, gift_card, crypto_transfer, irreversible. Unknown categories are scored as unknown risk, not rejected.

purpose.description: Short human description. Used as the category when category is omitted. Rewording it does not change a v1 verdict.

merchant.description: Merchant name or https endpoint URL that would receive the spend. The call does not pay this URL.

endpoint.description: Alias of merchant when the payee is an API URL. Pass one of them, not both for different payees.

agent_id.description: Your agent or key id. Echoed back, not scored in v1.

api_key.description: Optional SpendGate key (sg_live_…). Not a Toolweather tw_ key; that key belongs in the X-API-Key header. Omit to use the anonymous IP/session cap, which can reset on rotating egress.

daily_budget_remaining.description: USD still available today. Amount above this is blocked. Omit if you have no daily cap to enforce.

monthly_budget_remaining.description: USD still available this month. Amount above this is blocked. Omit if you have no monthly cap.

risk_hints.description: Self-reported hints. Raising: new_payee, new_merchant, first_payment, high_velocity, mismatched_purpose, off_platform, shared_wallet. Lowering: trusted_repeat, within_policy, human_preapproved. known_merchant marks the payee known.

tools.name: get_quota
tools.title: SpendGate free scores left today
tools.description: Read how many free SpendGate scores this caller has left today. Use before a run of score_spend calls. Do not use it for the Toolweather health-check quota, and do not use it to mint a key (spendgate_get_api_key or get_api_key). Does not consume a score and is not billed. Pass an sg_live_ key to read that key's cap; omit it only for the anonymous IP/session cap, which can reset on rotating egress. A tw_ key does not select this cap. Returns the remaining SpendGate count only.

api_key.description: Optional sg_live_ key from spendgate_get_api_key. Not a Toolweather tw_ key. Omit only to read the anonymous IP/session cap, which can reset on rotating egress.

tools.name: spendgate_get_api_key
tools.title: Get a free SpendGate API key
tools.description: Mint one new SpendGate API key (sg_live_…) for score_spend and get_quota. Use it once, then pass the secret as api_key on those tools. Do not call it every turn, and do not use it when you need a Toolweather key for health checks and watches (get_api_key returns tw_…). No required arguments. Each call creates a different secret. Returns that secret once. Not billed, and not drawn from the Toolweather quota. label is an optional stored note, not an auth secret.

label.description: Optional note stored beside the new sg_live_ key, max 80 characters. Not a secret and not a Toolweather key.
